judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The page's only h1 is "Lojas Renner S.A.", in small 10px text below the main carousel and above "DESTAQUES DO AQUECE BLACK FRIDAY". The live server-rendered HTML has the same h1. Everything under it is the store's home page: Black Friday highlights, trends, new arrivals, partner brands. A top-level heading that names the store on its own home page describes the page's topic. 2.4.6 asks only that headings describe topic or purpose, not that they summarise every section, and the h2s below do that for their sections. So the claim that it "says nothing about the content under it" does not hold. Small size and placement are not 2.4.6 issues. Rampa had all of this context and judged wrongly.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The "previous slider" arrow of the partner-brands carousel. Its class includes slick-disabled because the carousel starts at the first slide. The measured #e0e0e0 on white (1.32:1) is the disabled style. The "next slider" arrow, which is active, measures #191927 at 17.36:1 in the same snapshot. The screenshot shows the left arrow faint and the right one dark. In react-slick, a disabled arrow at slide 0 of a non-infinite carousel gets no click handler, so the control is visible but not currently operable. 1.4.11 exempts inactive components, and its Understanding document says they "are not required to meet contrast requirements". So the icon does not fail 1.4.11 in this state. Once the user advances, it turns dark. Not exposing the disabled state programmatically (no disabled or aria-disabled) would be a 4.1.2 matter, not a contrast failure. Users get the same initial state.
